chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Muawiya was the first to hang two shutters on his door in Makkah.'
So he prevented the pilgrims of the House of Allah from what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Equal is the one who dwells in it and the one who visits it.'
And the people, when they arrived in Makkah, the visitor would lodge with the dweller until he fulfilled his Hajj.
And Muawiya was the owner of the chain of which Allah the Exalted spoke: 'A chain whose length is seventy cubits, thrust him into it.'
'Surely he did not believe in Allah, the Magnificent,' and he was the Pharaoh of this community.

key_terms.حَاجَّ بَيْتِ اللَّهِ: Pilgrims of the House of Allah
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَة: Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan, the Umayyad Caliph

ai.seo_question: Who was the Pharaoh of this Ummah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Muawiya as the first to install double doors on the Ka'bah, a structural change that symbolized the Umayyad monopolization of religious authority and the exclusion of the common pilgrim. This act is theologically linked to the 'chain of seventy cubits' in Surah al-Haqqa, casting Muawiya as the 'Pharaoh of this Ummah' who bound the people to his rule, a concept deeply resonant in Shia historiography regarding the shift from communal access to dynastic control.
